tools.description: Search the public web for pages such as documentation, articles, release notes and discussions. Returns numbered results with title, url, the published date when known, and a short excerpt. Each search costs money. Don't use it to find source code: it can't match exact identifiers, file paths, commit SHAs or a pinned version, and usually returns nothing useful for them. Read the code on disk, or use a code search tool, instead. Use include_domains to restrict to sites (bare hostnames such as example.com) and recency to limit results to recently published pages.

include_domains.description: Only return results from these sites, as bare hostnames (example.com, not https://example.com/).

recency.description: Only return pages published within this period.

tools.name: web_search

tools.description: Search literal code patterns across about a million public GitHub repositories. Searches the default branch only. It cannot search private repositories, a pinned version or tag, or docs.rs. Read those from disk instead. Use query "pub fn with_capacity" with language ["Rust"], or query "func NewReader(" with repo "golang/go". Replies include repository, path and numbered lines. Caps are 20 file matches, 100 lines per file and 32 KiB of text.

language.description: Restrict to these language names, such as Rust or TypeScript.

path.description: Restrict file paths by partial match.

query.description: Literal code pattern to find. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; blank queries are refused.

regex.description: Interpret query as a regular expression.

repo.description: Restrict repositories by partial owner/repo name.

tools.name: code_search
